summary: Establishes normative script policy: POSIX shell by default; PowerShell only when Windows support is explicit
migration_impact: PLATE repositories now default to POSIX shell scripts only. PowerShell scripts are provided when a project explicitly declares Windows support. Template payload ships both as reference implementation since PLATE itself supports Windows operators.
migration_guidance: 1. Review your project's platform support stance: no explicit Windows requirement = POSIX-only, explicit Windows support = dual-stack (.sh + .ps1), Windows-only = .ps1 only.
2. If your project does not require Windows support, you may safely omit .ps1 scripts from new repositories created from this template.
3. When creating new scripts, agents must check project platform support first: default projects get .sh only, Windows-supported projects get both .sh (primary) and .ps1 (equivalent).
4. Platform support must come from human-stated project intent (SPEC.md, .plate config, onboarding answers, explicit instruction) — never inferred from developer OS or CI platform.
5. Existing dual-stack repositories (PLATE itself, template-derived repos with Windows support) may continue shipping both .sh and .ps1 without migration.
agent_notes: When authoring or modifying scripts: (1) Check if the project explicitly declares Windows support via SPEC.md, .plate config, or bootstrap answers. (2) Default (no platform stated) = ship .sh only. (3) Windows-supported (explicit) = ship both .sh (primary) and .ps1 (equivalent behavior). (4) Windows-only (explicit) = .ps1 only. Never infer platform support from developer laptop OS, Windows dependencies, or CI choices. PLATE's own template payload ships dual scripts as reference implementation for Windows-supported projects.
